target.title: fix(tool-payload): reject oversized XML parameters when text is multibyte
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where plain-text tool-call repair could accept serialized XML parameter blocks whose UTF-8 payload exceeded `maxPayloadBytes` when the parameter text contained multibyte characters. The JSON repair path already enforced byte-based limits, but the XML parameter path compared UTF-16 string length.

## Why This Change Was Made

The XML parameter reader now checks UTF-8 byte length for both per-parameter and cumulative XML payload limits, preserving the existing fast length rejection and parser behavior. This stays within the existing tool-payload boundary and does not add config, public API, or broader parser policy.

## User Impact

Tool-call repair now rejects oversized XML-style tool payloads consistently for ASCII and multibyte text, preventing over-limit tool arguments from being promoted into executable tool calls.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: serialized XML parameter tool-call repair rejects multibyte payloads over `maxPayloadBytes` while the existing parser behavior remains covered.
- Current-head proof at `250677bf1e8aabdd3a8ea6d44a6c86a276ec0b82`: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts` passed with 1 test file and 23 tests.
- Committed diff hygiene: `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD` passed.
- Review proof: `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode commit --commit HEAD` passed with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Observed result: the regression drives a serialized XML parameter with fewer UTF-16 code units than the 64-byte cap but more than 64 UTF-8 bytes, and `parseStandalonePlainTextToolCallBlocks` returns `null`.
